docs.title: vergil-fixture-python-lib
docs.text: This is a Vergil test fixture. It has no users. It is a small, real Python library that Vergil manages exactly as it manages any other library repo, so that a change to Vergil can be driven through it end to end before the change reaches a repo that matters.

docs.title: What it exercises
docs.text:
A fixture run takes the repo through Vergil's full cycle: a change, its PR and CI, the merge, a release, and a check of the result. On the way it exercises:

  • the Python vrg-validate gate: ruff, mypy, ty, pytest at 100% branch coverage, pip-audit and the license check;
  • CI on every Python version in the version window, as a library gets;
  • the dependency updater, Dependabot alerts and the vulnerability audit, through two real runtime dependencies, rich and packaging;
  • the tagged release and this documentation site.

Nothing it does reaches a package registry: it is never published to PyPI.

The program grows by one small function per fixture run. Each public function lives in a module of its own name, so a new one is a new module, a new test file and one line in the package's __init__.py.

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text: The design is in the language fixture repos spec (epic vergil-project/.github#1091).

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Getting Started: depend on it and validate it.
  • API: the public functions and how to call them.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Every public function is importable from the package itself:

from vergil_fixture_python_lib import (
    compare_versions,
    greet,
    is_prerelease,
    latest_version,
    render_table,
)

Each function raises on bad input rather than returning a placeholder.

docs.title: greet(name)
docs.text:
Returns a greeting, with the name's surrounding whitespace stripped.

>>> greet("Ada")
'Hello, Ada'

Raises ValueError when the name is empty or only whitespace.

docs.title: compare_versions(left, right)
docs.text:
Compares two PEP 440 version strings, using packaging. Returns -1, 0 or 1 as left is lower than, equal to or higher than right.

>>> compare_versions("1.2.0", "1.10.0")
-1
>>> compare_versions("2.0", "2.0.0")
0

Raises packaging.version.InvalidVersion when either string is not a PEP 440 version.

docs.title: latest_version(versions)
docs.text:
Returns the highest PEP 440 version in an iterable of strings, spelt as given. Of equal versions, the first one wins.

>>> latest_version(["1.2.0", "1.10.0", "1.9.9"])
'1.10.0'

Raises ValueError when there are no versions, and packaging.version.InvalidVersion when a string is not a PEP 440 version.

docs.title: is_prerelease(version)
docs.text:
Returns whether a PEP 440 version string is a pre-release (alpha, beta or release candidate) or a development release. A final release and a post-release are not.

>>> is_prerelease("2.0.0rc1")
True
>>> is_prerelease("1.0.post1")
False

Raises packaging.version.InvalidVersion when the string is not a PEP 440 version.

docs.title: render_table(title, headers, rows)
docs.text:
Renders a mapping as a two-column ASCII table with rich, as plain text with no terminal escapes. Each key is one row, in the mapping's order.

>>> print(render_table("Versions", ("Name", "Version"), {"rich": "14.0", "uv": "0.13"}), end="")
     Versions
+----------------+
| Name | Version |
|------+---------|
| rich | 14.0    |
| uv   | 0.13    |
+----------------+

Raises ValueError when rows is empty.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
The library is not on PyPI. Depend on a release tag (v<version>) straight from GitHub:

uv add 'vergil-fixture-python-lib @ git+https://github.com/vergil-project/vergil-fixture-python-lib@<tag>'

It needs Python 3.12 or later, and installs rich and packaging with it.

docs.title: Validating a change
docs.text:
Work in a worktree of the repo and run the one validation command:

vrg-container-run -- vrg-validate

It runs lint, type checks, the tests at 100% branch coverage and the dependency audit in the Python dev container.

docs.title: Adding a function
docs.text:
Each fixture run adds one function:

  1. Write tests/test_<name>.py with the expected values.
  2. Add src/vergil_fixture_python_lib/<name>.py holding the function.
  3. Import it in src/vergil_fixture_python_lib/__init__.py and add it to __all__, and to the list in tests/test_public_api.py.
  4. Document it on the API page.
